text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Disy chairman Yiannakis Matsis drops a bombshell: He accuses president Glafcos Clerides' daughter Katy of running against the party on its positions on the Cyprus problem.
- Military unmanning of sentry posts in close proximity is a priority for the United Nations peacekeeping force in Cyprus.
- Government expresses satisfaction over strong condemnation by U.N. Security Council over latest killing of an unarmed Greek Cypriot.
- Jobs could go as the pullout of Swedish packaging company Tetra Pak is confirmed.
- Parliamentarians agree on giving 18-year-olds the right to vote in all elections, but express concern the Supreme Court could strike the bill down as unconstitutional.

- Government keeps its distance from House of Representatives president Spyros Kyprianou, earlier quoted as saying Britain is looking at changes to the political system in the framework of a solution to the Cyprus problem.
- Akel describes government move to suspend petrol company surcharge 'provocative'.
- Britain's envoy on the Cyprus problem David Hannay shapes up ideas on the political system and on future guarantees for the island's independence.
- The European Union toned down its condemnation of Sunday's killing of a civilian by Turkish soldiers after intervention from Britain.
- Disy chairman Yiannakis Matsis says he is being 'undermined' by people within the party.
- The government and petrol companies are on a collision course over the price of petrol.
- Turkish Cypriot university professor Niazi Kizilyurek and president's daughter Katy Clerides deny having an affair.
